components.title: Uploaded company data, by policy
components.text: Bans alone don't work. People need tools, rules and training.

footnote: Source: University of Melbourne & KPMG, Trust, attitudes and use of AI: a global study 2025 (Apr 2025)
notes: Are these one-offs? Look at a survey of more than 32,000 employees in 47 countries, led by the University of Melbourne with KPMG, asking people who use AI at work. 48% admit uploading company information, such as financial, sales or customer data, to public AI tools. 66% have used AI output without evaluating it. 57% have hidden their use of AI or passed AI work off as their own. 56% have made mistakes at work because of AI, and 56% have used AI without knowing whether it was allowed. Now the number on the right: among staff whose company bans generative AI, the share who had uploaded company information was highest of all, at 67%. It was 56% where there's a usage policy and 33% where there's none. The report's conclusion: bans don't work on their own, and having a policy doesn't guarantee people follow it. People need clear guidance and training. That's why we're here today. Bear in mind these are self-reported, so the real figures may be higher. This is a corporate survey, led by a university.
